newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude prices firm, Tapis spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude prices firm, Tapis spreads widen.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were mostly firmer on Monday, supported by strong futures prices, with confirmation of October Tapis trading at a $1.00 premium.
A producer sold 300,000 barrels of mid-October lifting Tapis crude at a premium over published quotes of $1.00 per barrel to a Singapore refiner.
Traders said the firm number, which reflected strong demand for light sweet grades, stretched Nov/Dec and Dec/Jan paper spreads out to 35-40 cents from 20-25 cents late last week.
In late trading November Tapis was not bid but was offered at $23.55/$23.60 with a notional offer on October placed at $23.75.
Traders said 100,000 barrels of Minas was said traded into China at ICP plus 18 cents.
In wet markets, traders said there was talk a late October Oman was sold by a trader to a major at MPM less 57 cents. The deal was denied by the parties said to be involved.
A national oil company sold a late October cargo on Friday at MPM less 50 cents to a European major.

November Oman has traded at the equivalent of around MPM less 14 cents. An unconfirmed deal was done at MPM less two cents between majors late last week, but another version suggested a cargo was sold in a chain of a trader, U.S. refiner and a major.
The trader was said to be short of November Oman and was seen bidding the market at Dubai quotes plus 85 cents, traders said.
Elsewhere, traders said India's award of four Dubai cargos in its November tender was a cargo more than had been expected.
